Most people assume the great masters simply suffered.

Kevin Trudeau points out that Ram spent seven years in the wilderness and Jesus spent time in the desert. Everybody assumes that was a period of suffering and adversity.

But Kevin says if you read the texts, they never described it that way. They saw it as an opportunity, a change in circumstance that let them do something most people never get to do.

What if your hardest chapter is an opportunity you haven't recognised yet?

#ad #mindset #success

Your fear might just be a habit you can change.

Kevin Trudeau says people have a habit of thinking and a habit of speaking, and many of them think and speak out of fear.

He explains that once you become aware it's only a habit, you can change it. He was taught two words: cancel, cancel. That cancels the old thought, and then you replace it with a new habit of thought.

Kevin says that's how you handle life.

Which fearful thought do you repeat most often?

#ad #habits #mindset

Most people don't realise they can choose how they feel.

Kevin Trudeau says you can go through life choosing your thoughts, your words and your actions on purpose, and that lets you choose how you feel.

Imagine deciding to feel happy. Or giving anger one minute, then stopping.

Kevin says most people feel angry, sad or full of loss and never see they're in control. They let their mind control them.

When did you last feel truly in charge of your own mind?

#ad #mindset #happiness

Positive thinkers often skip this important step.

Kevin Trudeau says the spiritual masters did two things when hard times came. First, they acknowledged how they felt instead of denying it. Kevin says most people deny their feelings, especially positive thinkers who try to reframe everything.

Second, they welcomed the challenge instead of resisting it. What you resist will persist.

Are you resisting something in your life right now, or welcoming it?
